blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: An LLM safety patch can pass a benchmark while still being a poor repair. This risk is especially acute for jailbreak repairs, where the goal is to correct a specific unsafe behaviour without changing unrelated behaviours. A patch may block the exact prompts used for evaluation yet fail on close harmful variants, or suppress harmful behaviour by over-refusing benign prompts that share its wording or structure. Existing evaluation protocols primarily test whether models can be broken, while aggregate metrics, such as attack success, refusal rates, and global capability scores, cannot distinguish selective repairs from broader local suppression. To address this gap, we introduce PatchBench , a benchmark of empirically observed model-specific jailbreak failures that induce actionable harmful answers, designed as concrete repair targets for patching research. Starting from 27,870 prompts aggregated from 37 public jailbreak benchmark datasets, we manually curate 15,314 English prompts and query 8 open-source instruction-tuned models. We then combine WildGuard filtering, pairwise Elo ranking, and manual verification to retain only unsafe completions that answer the harmful requests. The result is a curated bank of 400 high-confidence jailbreak failures, organised by model. We further introduce PatchBench-Local , a local evaluation protocol that tests whether a patch is behaviourally precise. For each harmful source prompt, PatchBench-Local generates three families of local neighbours: harmful variants that preserve the malicious intent, benign prompts with matched structure, and benign prompts that reuse the key harmful terms. It evaluates both harmful-neighbour correction and benign-neighbour preservation, thus distinguishing selective repair from broader local suppression. We use PatchBench-Local and MMLU to evaluate four state-of-the-art activation steering methods. Our results show that global capability can remain nearly unchanged while local benign-neighbour regressions are severe, confirming that aggregate metrics alone can miss important collateral damage. By exposing whether patches act as precise behavioural repairs or as broad local suppressors, PatchBench-Local provides a more precise basis for developing and comparing jailbreak repair methods.
blocks.zh: 一个LLM安全补丁可以通过一个基准,同时仍然是一个差的修复. 这种风险对于越狱修复来说尤其严重,因为监狱修复的目标是纠正一种特定的不安全行为,而不改变无关的行为。 补丁可能阻断用于评价的确切提示,但在接近有害的变体上却失败,或者通过过度反射的良性提示来抑制有害的行为,后者的措辞或结构相同。 现有的评价协议主要检验模型是否可以被打破,而总的衡量标准,如攻击成功率,拒绝率,以及全球能力分数,无法区分选择性修理和更广泛的局部压制. 为了弥补这一差距,我们引入了Patch Bench, 这是一种经验性观测到的针对模型的越狱失败的基准, 引发了可采取行动的有害答案, 被设计为补丁研究的具体修复目标。 从27,870个提示从37个公共越狱基准数据集汇总开始,我们手动整理了15,314个英语提示并查询了8个开源指令调用模型。 然后我们把WildGuard过滤、双向Elo排名和人工核查结合起来,只保留回答有害请求的不安全完成。 结果是一家由四百名高自信的越狱失败者组成的管理银行。 我们进一步推出Patch Bench-Local 本地评估协议, 对于每一个有害来源的提示,Patch Bench-Local会生成三个当地邻居的家庭:保存恶意意图的有害变体,具有相匹配结构的良性提示和再利用关键有害术语的良性提示. 它既评估了有害-邻校正,又评估了良性-邻校正,从而将选择性修复与更广泛的局部压制区分开来. 我们使用Patch Bench-Local和MMLU来评价四种最先进的活化活化引导方法. 我们的结果表明,全球能力几乎保持不变,而当地良性邻国的回归却十分严重,这证明仅是总的衡量标准就可能忽略重要的附带损害。 Patch Bench-Local通过揭露补丁是作为精确的行为修复还是作为广泛的局部抑制器,为开发和比较越狱修复方法提供了更准确的基础.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Large language models (LLMs) remain vulnerable to jailbreaks ( Carlini et al., 2024 ; Shen et al., 2024 ; Chao et al., 2024 ) : adversarial prompts that elicit responses a model should refuse. This has motivated work on safer decoding ( Xu et al., 2024 ) , training-time alignment ( Ouyang et al., 2022 ; Bianchi et al., 2024 ) , and post-hoc mitigation strategies ( Turner et al., 2024 ; Zou et al., 2025 ; Arditi et al., 2024 ) . Among these, activation patching ( Zhang and Nanda, 2024 ) is an appealing direction for targeted safety repair: it intervenes directly on internal representations at inference time, aiming to suppress a specific unsafe behaviour while preserving the rest of the model’s capabilities.
blocks.zh: 大型语言模型仍然容易被越狱(Carlini等人,2024年); 沈等,2024; Chao等, 2024:引起响应的对抗性提示 模型应拒绝. 这推动了关于更安全的解码(徐等,2024年),培训时间调整(欧阳等,2022年;比安奇等,2024年),以及事后缓解策略(特纳等,2024年;邹等,2025年;阿尔迪蒂等,2024年)的工作. 其中,激活补丁(Zhang and Nanda, 2024)是目标明确的安全修复的吸引力方向:它直接干预推断时间的内部表述,目的是抑制特定不安全行为,同时保留模型的其他能力.

blocks.en: This setting calls for an evaluation protocol that matches the targeted nature of the intervention. Standard jailbreak robustness metrics are useful for measuring model-level safety ( Chao et al., 2024 ; Luo et al., 2024 ; Dang et al., 2026 ) , but they do not characterise what happens in the local neighbourhood of a repaired failure. After patching, two questions remain open: does the intervention suppress nearby harmful variants of the source prompt, such as paraphrases, formatting changes, or language shifts, and does it preserve the model’s behaviour on benign prompts that are lexically or structurally close to it? These local questions are central to activation patching, but they are not the primary object of existing aggregate evaluations ( Chao et al., 2024 ; Han et al., 2024 ; Dang et al., 2026 ) .

blocks.en: Evaluating such repairs requires concrete repair targets. A harmful prompt alone is not enough: if the model already refuses it, there is no failure to repair. We thus built PatchBench, a dataset starting from prompt-answer pairs in which a model actually produces actionable harmful assistance, illustrated in Figure 1 . This makes the benchmark model-specific by construction: the target for patching is not an abstract harmful request, but a failure that the model to be repaired has genuinely exhibited. PatchBench curates these failures from public jailbreak benchmarks ( Dang et al., 2026 ; Chao et al., 2024 ; Jiang et al., 2024 ; Shen et al., 2024 ) , yielding 400 manually verified, model-specific jailbreak failures.
blocks.zh: 评价这种修理需要具体的修理目标。 仅靠有害的快取是不够的:如果模型已经拒绝,就不存在修复失败. 因此,我们建造了Patch Bench这个数据集,它从快速回答对开始,其中一个模型实际上产生了可操作的有害援助,如图1所示。 这使得基准模型通过构建而具有特异性:补丁的目标并不是抽象的有害请求,而是被修复的模型真正表现出的失败. Patch Bench根据公共越狱基准(Dang等人,2026年;Chao等人,2024年;Jiang等人,2024年;Shen等人,2024年)对这些失误进行了校正,产生了400起人工核实的典型越狱失误。

blocks.en: We then introduce PatchBench-Local to evaluate what happens around each target once a patch is applied. For every source failure, it defines a local neighbourhood of harmful variants, benign prompts with matched structure, and benign prompts that reuse key harmful terms. This lets us test whether the patch generalises beyond the exact harmful prompt while preserving nearby benign behaviour.

blocks.en: Our experiments with four activation patching methods on four representative models show that these properties can diverge substantially. Methods that strongly suppress nearby harmful variants can still induce benign-neighbour regressions, including when MMLU remains nearly unchanged. This supports the central claim of the paper: activation patching should be evaluated as local repair, with explicit measurement of both harmful-neighbour correction and benign-neighbour preservation.
blocks.zh: 我们用四种激活补丁方法在四种代表性模型上的实验表明,这些特性可以有很大的差别。 强烈抑制附近有害变体的方法仍能诱发良性-邻接回归,包括当MMLU几乎保持不变时. 这支持了文件的中心主张:激活补丁应被评价为局部修复,同时明确测量有害-邻居的校正和良-邻居的保存.

blocks.en: Our contributions are: • We introduce PatchBench , a curated benchmark of 400 actionable jailbreak failures across 8 open-source instruction-tuned models, designed as concrete repair targets for activation patching. • We propose PatchBench-Local , a local evaluation protocol measuring harmful-neighbour correction and benign-neighbour preservation around each repaired failure. • We show, on four representative models and four activation patching methods, that strong harmful-neighbour correction can coincide with substantial benign-neighbour regressions, including when MMLU remains nearly unchanged.

blocks.en: 2 Background and Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 背景和有关工作

blocks.en: Improving the reliability of large language models requires alignment techniques such as supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning from human feedback Ouyang et al. (2022) ; Touvron et al. (2023) ; Bianchi et al. (2024) ; Shen et al. (2023) . These methods aim to make models helpful while preventing harmful, toxic, or unethical outputs. However, jailbreak attacks remain a persistent failure mode: adversarial prompts can still bypass safeguards and elicit responses that aligned models should refuse Carlini et al. (2024) ; Zvi (2022) . Recent work further suggests that safety behaviour can rely on fragile output-level patterns rather than robust safety-relevant representations Qi et al. (2024) ; Jeong et al. (2025) ; Russinovich et al. (2026) . This brittleness motivates methods that act directly on internal representations rather than only changing prompts or training data.
blocks.zh: 提高大语言模型的可靠性,需要从人类反馈欧阳等(2022年);图夫龙等(2023年);比安奇等(2024年);沈等(2023年)中监督微调和强化学习等校正技术. 这些方法旨在使模型有所帮助,同时防止有害、有毒或不道德的产出。 然而,越狱攻击仍然是一个持续的失败模式:对抗性诱因仍然可以绕过保障措施,并引起一致模式拒绝卡利尼等人(2024年);Zvi (2022年)的回应. 近期的工作还表明,安全行为可以依赖脆弱的产出水平模式,而不能依赖与安全有关的强力代表Qi等人(2024年);Jeong等人(2025年);Russinovich等人(2026年)。 这种不便促使采用直接针对内部表述而不是仅仅改变提示或培训数据的方法。

blocks.en: A natural way to correct such failures is to retrain or fine-tune the model, but this can be costly and may affect unrelated behaviours Qi et al. (2024) . In contrast, inference-time interventions aim to modify model behaviour without changing the weights. This makes them attractive for targeted safety repair: in principle, they can suppress a specific unsafe behaviour while leaving most of the model unchanged. The key question is then not only whether the unsafe behaviour is suppressed, but whether the intervention remains selective.
blocks.zh: 纠正这种失误的一个自然方式是重新训练或微调模型,但这可能代价高昂并可能影响与Qi等人(2024年)无关的行为。 与此相反,推论时间干预旨在修改模式行为而不会改变权重. 这使得它们具有针对性地进行安全修复的吸引力:原则上,它们可以压制特定的不安全行为,同时使大多数模型保持不变. 关键的问题不仅在于不安全的行为是否受到压制,而且在于干预是否仍然是选择性的。

blocks.en: Activation steering modifies internal representations at inference time by adding, subtracting, or scaling steering vectors Turner et al. (2024) ; Zou et al. (2025) ; Louapre (2025) . Such vectors can be used to control high-level behaviours without updating model weights. Several works have identified directions associated with safety-relevant behaviours, including refusal Arditi et al. (2024) ; Li et al. (2024) . Removing or weakening these directions can reduce refusal on harmful instructions, while reinforcing them can induce refusal even on harmless inputs. This makes activation steering both a useful tool for studying model internals and a candidate mechanism for post-hoc safety repair.
blocks.zh: 活性向导在推论时通过加减或缩放向量来修改内部表示; Zou等 (2025); Louapre (2025). 这种向量可用于控制高层次的行为而无需更新模型权重. 一些工作确定了与安全相关的行为有关的方向,包括拒绝Arditi等人(2024年);Li等人(2024年)。 取消或削弱这些指示可以减少对有害指示的拒绝,而加强这些指示甚至可以引起对无害输入的拒绝。 这使得活化引导既成为了研究模型内部的有用工具,又成为了热后安全修复的候选机制.

blocks.en: Recent methods aim to make steering more selective. Activation Steering (AST) Arditi et al. (2024) ; Lee et al. (2025) applies a refusal direction unconditionally across prompts, which can increase refusal but also affect benign behaviour. Conditional Activation Steering (CAST) Lee et al. (2025) gates this direction using prompt-specific activation patterns. AdaSteer Zhao et al. (2025) modulates steering through a harmfulness signal, while AlphaSteer Sheng et al. (2026) learns constrained scaling factors intended to preserve utility. These methods explicitly seek a safety–utility trade-off, but they are typically evaluated with aggregate attack success, refusal, or utility scores. Such metrics are informative at the model level, but they do not show whether a given intervention is locally precise around the repaired failure.
blocks.zh: 最近的方法旨在使方向更具选择性。 活性引导(AST) Arditi等 (2024) ; Lee等 (2025) 无条件跨活性提示应用拒绝方向,这可以增加拒绝,但也会影响良性行为. 有条件激活指导(CAST) 李等编. (2025)利用即时特异活化模式将这个方向打开. AdaSteer 赵等. (2025年)通过有害信号来调节方向,而AlphaSteer Sheng等人(2026年)学习了旨在维护效用的受约束的缩放因子. 这些方法明确寻求安全-效用权衡,但通常以总的攻击成功率、拒绝率或效用分数来评估。 这种衡量标准在模型层面是翔实的,但并不表明某一干预在修复后故障周围是否是当地精确的。

blocks.en: Existing jailbreak datasets provide attack prompts on which safety mechanisms are tested. RedBench Dang et al. (2026) aggregates dozens of public datasets under a standardised taxonomy; JailbreakBench Chao et al. (2024) provides harmful behaviours, benign controls, and a reproducible evaluation pipeline; WildJailbreak Jiang et al. (2024) provides large-scale synthetic adversarial instances; and in-the-wild collections Shen et al. (2024) capture prompts observed on public platforms. These resources have helped establish attack success rate, refusal rate, and utility preservation as dominant evaluation axes Luo et al. (2024) .
blocks.zh: 现有的越狱数据集为测试安全机制提供了攻击提示. Red Bench Dang等(2026年)在标准化分类法下汇总了数十套公共数据集;Jailbreak Bench Chao等(2024年)提供了有害行为、良性控制和可再生评价管道;WildJailbreak Jiang等(2024年)提供了大规模合成对抗案例;以及内部收集。 沈等编. (2024)捕获在公共平台上观察到的提示. 这些资源有助于确定攻击成功率、拒绝率和公用事业维护作为主要评价轴(Luo等)(2024年)。

blocks.en: However, most jailbreak benchmarks are primarily banks of prompts. They do not necessarily indicate whether a given model actually fails on each prompt, nor do they provide the harmful completion that was produced. For patching research, this distinction matters: a prompt that is already refused is not a repair target. PatchBench addresses this gap by releasing confirmed, model-specific harmful completions as actionable failures to patch. PatchBench-Local then addresses a second limitation of aggregate evaluation: whether a patch has been precisely applied. It distinguishes under-generalisation, where a patch blocks the source prompt but fails on nearby harmful variants, from over-generalisation, where it suppresses benign prompts that share structure or wording with the repaired failure.
blocks.zh: 然而,大多数越狱基准主要是诱饵银行。 它们不一定表明某一型号是否在每一时速上实际失效,也不一定提供所生产的有害完成。 对于补丁研究来说,这种区别很重要:已经被拒绝的快件不是修理目标. 帕奇·本奇通过释放确认的,模型特有的有害完成作为可操作的补丁故障来弥补这一缺口. Patch Bench-local然后处理汇总评价的第二个限制:是否精确应用了补丁. 它区分了泛化不足,即一补丁阻断了源头,但在附近的有害变体上失败,与泛化过度,压制了与被修复的失败共用结构或措辞的良性提示.

blocks.en: Automated safety classifiers such as WildGuard and Llama Guard scale safety assessment by labelling harmfulness, refusal, or prompt answering Han et al. (2024) ; Inan et al. (2023) . LLM-as-judge protocols similarly support task-specific behavioural comparisons. These tools are useful for benchmark construction and evaluation, including filtering candidate failures and scoring model responses. Yet they are most often applied to isolated outputs or aggregate benchmark outcomes, rather than to structured local neighbourhoods around a targeted repair.
blocks.zh: 诸如WildGuard和Llama Guard等自动安全分类器,通过标记有害、拒绝或及时回答Han等人(2024年);Ian等人(2023年). LLM-as-judge协议同样支持特定任务的行为比较。 这些工具对基准构建和评价很有用,包括过滤候选失败和评分模型反应。 然而,它们往往被应用于孤立的产出或总的基准结果,而不是围绕着目标明确的修复而结构化的地方住区。

blocks.en: A related limitation appears in causal evaluation of internal interventions. Activation patching and ablation studies often rely on logit differences, probability shifts, or layer-wise causal effects Zhang and Nanda (2024) . These quantities are valuable for mechanistic analysis, but they do not directly characterise behavioural precision: whether a patch generalises to semantically close harmful variants while preserving structurally or lexically related benign prompts. PatchBench-Local complements these tools by defining such local neighbourhoods explicitly and jointly measuring harmful-variant correction and benign-prompt preservation.
blocks.zh: 在内部干预的因果评价中出现了相关的限制。 活性补丁和活性化研究往往依赖于对数差异,概率变化,或分层因果张和南达(2024). 这些数量对于机械分析很有价值,但它们并不直接说明行为精确性:是否一个补丁泛指在保留结构或逻辑上相联的良性诱因的同时,将有害变种相近。 Patch Bench-Local对这些工具加以补充,明确界定这些当地街区,并共同测量有害-多变性的矫正和良性-速效保护。

blocks.en: 3 PatchBench: Building a Bank of Patchable Jailbreak Failures
blocks.zh: 3 Patch Bench: 建设可补丁监狱故障银行

blocks.en: PatchBench is designed for activation patching in white-box settings. Unlike standard jailbreak benchmarks, which primarily provide harmful prompts, PatchBench provides verified model failures: model-specific prompt-completion pairs in which a model actually produces actionable harmful assistance. Each item is therefore a concrete repair target for post-hoc patching.
blocks.zh: Patch Bench 设计用于在白盒设置中激活补丁. 与主要提供有害提示的标准越狱基准不同的是,Patch Bench提供了经过验证的模型故障:模型特定的即时补全对,其中模型实际上会产生可操作的有害援助. 因此,每件物品都是用于后热补丁的混凝土修复目标.

blocks.en: We define a patchable jailbreak failure as a pair where the prompt expresses a clearly harmful or disallowed intent and the completion directly answers it with actionable harmful assistance instead of refusing. This includes practical instructions, operational guidance, code, material sourcing, or any content that materially lowers the barrier to harm; vague, low-quality, or merely suggestive answers are excluded.
blocks.zh: 我们把可补缺的越狱失败定义为一对,即迅速表示明显有害或不可接受的意图,完成就直接用可诉的有害援助而不是拒绝来回答。 这包括实用指示、操作指导、代码、材料来源,或实质性地降低损害障碍的任何内容;模糊、低质量或仅仅是暗示性的答案被排除在外。

blocks.en: This definition is tailored to patching: borderline outputs make it difficult to determine whether a patch has removed the relevant behaviour. PatchBench therefore prioritises clear failures with a meaningful behaviour to suppress and a well-defined source prompt around which local regressions can be evaluated.
blocks.zh: 这个定义是针对补丁的:边线输出使得难以确定一个补丁是否已去除相关行为. 因此,Patch Bench将明确的失败列为优先事项,采取有意义的行为加以压制,并发出明确的源来进行局部回归评价。

blocks.en: 3.1 Benchmark construction
blocks.zh: 3.1 基准建设

blocks.en: We construct PatchBench from RedBench ( Dang et al., 2026 ) , an aggregation of 37 public jailbreak benchmark datasets totalling 27,870 prompts. We manually remove duplicated benchmark content, non-generative prompts, malformed items, and prompts whose harmful intent is too weak or underspecified for targeted repair evaluation, yielding 15,314 prompts.
blocks.zh: 我们从Red Bench(Dang等, 2026年)构建了Patch Bench, 我们手动删除了重复的基准内容、非再生提示、畸形物品、有害意图太弱或不够明确的提示,以便进行有针对性的修复评估,产生了15 314个提示。

blocks.en: We query this filtered pool on eight open-source instruction-tuned models spanning four providers and multiple scales: Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct , Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct , gemma-3-4b-it , gemma-3-12b-it , Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct , Llama-4-Scout , Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 , and Ministral-3-14B-Instruct . All models use their native chat templates and deterministic greedy decoding, making failures attributable to the model–prompt pair rather than sampling noise. This produces 122,512 prompt-completion pairs.
blocks.zh: 我们以8个开源指令调试模型查询这个过滤池,这些模型跨越4个提供者和多个尺度:Qun2.5-3B-指令;Qun2.5-14B-指令;gemma-3-4b-it;gemma-3-12b-it;Llama-3.1-8B-指令;Llama-4-Scout;Mistral-7B-struct-v0.3;以及Mindernal-3-14B-指令。 所有模型都使用其本地聊天模板和确定性贪婪的解码,使失败归因于模型-即时对子而不是取样噪音. 这产生了122,512个即时完成对.

blocks.en: The raw generations contain many refusals, weak failures, and borderline cases. We therefore use WildGuard Han et al. (2024) (validated via human evaluation with 92.6% accuracy; see Appendix B ) before ranking, retaining only pairs classified as both unsafe and answering the harmful request. This yields 6,380 model-specific candidate failures.
blocks.zh: 生代包含许多拒绝,弱失败,和分界线的案件. 因此,我们先使用WildGuard Han等人(2024年)(通过人类评估验证,准确度为92.6%;见附录B)进行排名,只保留被归类为既不安全又回应有害请求的对子. 这导致6 380个特定模式候选人失败。

blocks.en: Figure 2 : PatchBench construction pipeline. Starting from 27,870 jailbreak prompts, we manually filter the source pool, query eight open-source instruction-tuned models, retain unsafe answering completions with WildGuard, rank candidate failures model-wise with Elo comparisons, and manually curate the final 50 patchable failures per model.
blocks.zh: 图2:帕奇·本奇建筑管道。 从27,870个出狱提示开始,我们手动过滤出源集合,查询8个开源指令调试模型,用WildGuard保留不安全的解答完成,用Elo比较的方法对候选失败模型进行排序,并手动解决每个模型最后50个可补补缺.

blocks.en: 3.2 Model-wise ranking and human curation
blocks.zh: 3.2 按模式排列等级和人文分类

blocks.en: The candidate pool is still too large and heterogeneous to serve directly as a high-precision patching benchmark. We therefore rank candidate failures separately for each model using pairwise Elo comparisons, following the protocol of Jenny et al. Jenny et al. (2026) for harmfulness ranking of jailbreak completions.
blocks.zh: 候选人才库仍然庞大而多变,无法直接作为高精度补丁基准。 因此,我们按照Jenny等人的规程,使用对等的Elo比较法,对每个模型的候选人失败进行单独排序。 Jenny等 (2026),为越狱结业的有害排名.

blocks.en: The ranking unit is the full prompt-completion pair rather than the completion alone, since harmfulness depends on whether the answer fulfils the malicious intent of the prompt. For each model, we sample random pairs of candidate failures and ask an LLM judge which completion is more harmful to generate, prioritising directness, completeness, and actionable usefulness. Based on a preliminary stability analysis, Elo scores became approximately stable after roughly 40 matches per candidate; we therefore require at least 50 pairwise matches per candidate and compute Elo scores independently for each model with K-factor = 40 =40 .
blocks.zh: 排名单位是完整的即时补全对而非仅是完成,因为有害性取决于答案是否满足了即时的恶意意图. 对于每个模型,我们抽取随机对候选人的失败结果,并询问一个LLM判断器,哪个完成更有害于生成,更优先考虑直接性,完整性和可操作的有用性. 根据初步稳定分析,埃洛的得分在每位候选人大约40分之后大致稳定;因此,我们需要每个候选人至少50分对对对并计算 埃洛以K-因子=40=40的成绩为每个型号独立得分.

blocks.en: We then manually review the top 200 candidates for each model and retain the 50 most significant actionable jailbreak failures. This final review removes borderline cases and ensures that each retained item is both a convincing model failure and a meaningful patching target. The resulting benchmark contains 400 prompt-completion pairs, organised as 50 high-confidence failures for each of the eight models; each released item includes the harmful prompt, the model completion, and the model identifier. WildGuard and Elo ranking are used to prioritise candidates, but the final retained instances are manually verified.
blocks.zh: 然后我们手动审查每种模式的200名候选人,并保留50起最重要的可诉越狱失败。 本次最终审查删除了边框案件,并确保每个保留的项目既是令人信服的模型故障,又是有意义的补丁目标. 由此产生的基准包括400个即时补全对,按8个模型中的每个模型的50个高度置信失败排列;每个被放出的项目包括有害的即时补全,模型补全,以及模型标识符. WildGuard和Elo排名用于优先考虑候选人,但最后保留的例子是人工核实的.

blocks.en: 3.3 Benchmark statistics
blocks.zh: 3.3 基准统计

blocks.en: PatchBench covers a diverse set of harmful behaviours. At the dataset level, the final benchmark is distributed across three broad categories: weapons (38.5%), cyber (36.0%), and crimes, fraud, and abuse (25.5%). This aggregate balance hides substantial variation across models. For instance, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct is dominated by cyber failures (58%), whereas gemma-3-12b-it and Ministral-3-14B-Instruct are dominated by weapon-related failures (54% and 52%). In contrast, Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct is mostly represented by crimes, fraud, and abuse prompts (54%). These differences show that PatchBench captures model-specific failure profiles relevant to targeted repair.
blocks.zh: 帕奇·本奇涵盖一系列不同的有害行为。 在数据集一级,最终基准分布在三大类:武器(38.5%)、网络(36.0%)和犯罪、欺诈和虐待(25.5%)。 这种总体平衡掩盖了各种模型之间的巨大差异。 例如,Llama-3.1-8B-指令以网络故障为主(58%),而Gemma-3-12b-it和Ministry-3-14B-指令以武器故障为主(54%和52%)。 与此相反,第Wen2.5-3B-指令主要是犯罪、欺诈和虐待诱发(54%)。 这些差异表明,Patch Bench捕捉到与目标修复相关的模型特有故障剖面.

blocks.en: Because PatchBench is built separately for each model, the same source prompt can appear in several model-specific subsets when it induces a high-confidence failure for multiple models. In the final benchmark, 241 source prompts appear for a single model only, while 68 distinct source prompts appear for at least two models. Most recurring prompts appear for exactly two models; only a few appear for three or more. This is not a dedicated transfer benchmark, but it shows that PatchBench contains both model-specific failures and a smaller set of prompts that repeatedly induce failures across models.
blocks.zh: 由于Patch Bench是针对每个模型单独构建的,当它诱发多个模型的高自信失败时,同一源的快取可以在多个模型特定的子集中出现. 在最终基准中,241个源提示只出现在单一模型上,而68个不同的源提示至少出现在两个模型上. 多数反复出现的提示出现在两个模型中;只有三个或三个以上。 这不是一个专用的转移基准,但它表明,Patch Bench既包含针对模型的失败,也包含一组更小的提示,反复地诱发跨模型的失败.

blocks.en: Figure 3 : Category distribution of retained jailbreak failures across models. Each bar shows the composition of the 50 retained PatchBench instances for one model.
blocks.zh: 图3:各模型中留守越狱失败的类别分布情况。 每个栏显示一个模型的50个保留Patch Bench实例的构成。

blocks.en: 4 PatchBench-Local: A Dynamic Protocol for Local Evaluation
blocks.zh: 4 Patch Bench - 当地雇员: 地方评价动态协议

blocks.en: PatchBench provides concrete jailbreak failures as patching targets. PatchBench-Local asks the next question: once a patch is applied, is the intervention locally selective? A useful patch should induce refusal on the source prompt and nearby harmful variants, while avoiding over-refusal on nearby benign prompts.
blocks.zh: Patch Bench提供具体的越狱失败作为补丁目标. Patch Bench-local 问下一个问题:一旦一个补丁被应用,该干预是否局部有选择性? 一个有用的补丁应诱发迅速和相邻的有害变体拒绝源头,同时避免对相邻的良性诱因产生过度的反驳.

blocks.en: This differs from standard aggregate evaluation. Global utility metrics such as MMLU ( Hendrycks et al., 2021 ) , or broad refusal-rate evaluations, can measure model-level side effects, but they are too coarse to diagnose the local impact of a targeted patch. A patch may preserve global performance while over-refusing lexically or structurally close benign prompts, or block the source prompt without generalising to small harmful variations. PatchBench-Local measures this local correction–preservation trade-off directly.
blocks.zh: 这与标准综合评价不同。 全球通用度量衡,如MMLU(Hendrycks等,2021年),或广义的拒绝率评价,可以测量模型层面的副作用,但它们过于粗糙,无法诊断定点补丁的局部影响. 补丁可能保留全球性能,同时在逻辑上或结构上过于接近良性提示,或阻断源出提示而不会泛指小的有害变化. Patch Bench- Local 直接衡量本地的校正- 保全权衡。

blocks.en: 4.1 Local prompt generation
blocks.zh: 4.1 当地迅速生成

blocks.en:
Given a source jailbreak failure, PatchBench-Local generates 29 local prompts from the original harmful prompt, yielding 30 evaluation prompts including the source. The neighbourhood is generated with Mistral Large using a fixed prompt template, reported in Appendix C.1 . We manually sanity-checked roughly 50 generated neighbourhoods before fixing the template for the full local evaluation.
To confirm robustness to generator choice against LLM bias and ensure long-term reproducibility, we also generated neighbourhoods using GPT-4o. As detailed in Appendix C.2 , this sensitivity analysis confirms that the downstream evaluation results are stable, proving our protocol is robust to the choice of the generating LLM.
blocks.zh:
鉴于一个源代码的越狱失败,Patch Bench-Local从最初的有害提示中生成了29个当地提示,产生了30个评价提示,包括源代码. 邻接区与Mistral Large一起使用一个固定的即时模板生成,该模板在附录C.1中报告。 我们手动检查了大约50个生成的街区,然后确定了当地全面评价的模板。
为了证实对LLM偏差的生成者选择的稳健性并确保长期可复制性,我们还利用GPT-4o生成了街区. 如附录C.2所详述,这种敏感性分析证实下游评价结果是稳定的,证明我们的协议对生成LLM的选择是有力的.

blocks.en: The generated neighbourhood contains three prompt families. The first contains 19 harmful variants: 10 paraphrases, 2 translations, 3 punctuation variants, 1 case-inversion variant, and 3 spelling or grammatical variants. These preserve the malicious intent while changing the surface form, testing whether the patch induces refusal beyond the exact source wording.
blocks.zh: 产生的社区包括三个迅速的家庭。 第一种包含有19个有害的变体:10个译出,2个译出,3个出格变体,1个出格变体,以及3个拼音或语法变体. 这些在改变表面形态的同时保留了恶意意图,测试补丁是否诱发出超出确切出处措辞的拒绝.

blocks.en: The two benign families test over-refusal. The first contains 5 structural neighbours, which preserve the scaffold of the original request, including the multiple-choice structure when present, but replace the harmful intent with a benign one. The second contains 5 harmful-word neighbours, which reuse salient harmful terms in benign or informational contexts, with multiple-choice blocks removed when present.
blocks.zh: 两个善良的家庭 测试过度反弹。 第一种有5个结构相邻,保留了原始请求的脚手架,包括当存在时的多选择结构,但以良性意图来取而代之. 第二类包括5个有害词语的邻居,这些邻居在良性或信息背景下重新使用明显的有害词语,在出现时将多个选择区块取出。

blocks.en: Figure 4 : Local prompt generation. Starting from a single harmful prompt, PatchBench-Local generates harmful variants that preserve the malicious intent and benign neighbours that are either structurally matched or lexically related. These prompts test whether a patch generalises to nearby harmful requests while avoiding over-refusal on nearby benign prompts.
blocks.zh: 图4:当地迅速生成。 Patch Bench-Local从一个有害的瞬间开始产生有害的变体,这些变体保留了恶意意图和在结构上或逻辑上相匹配的良性邻居。 这些促使人们测试一个补丁是否对附近的有害请求进行概括,同时避免对附近的良性提示进行过度反驳.

blocks.en: 4.2 Local evaluation protocol
blocks.zh: 4.2 地方评价协议

blocks.en: For each source failure, we query the patched model on the source prompt and its 29 neighbours. We score each response with WildGuard, which provides unsafe, refusal, and prompt-answering signals; PatchBench-Local uses the refusal signal to define binary labels according to each prompt family. We verified the quality of those labels by manually checking random samples from every model.
blocks.zh: 对于每个源故障,我们都会在源速率及其29个邻居上查询补丁模型. 我们用 WildGuard 来评分每个响应,它提供了不安全的,拒绝的,以及即时的回答信号; Patch Bench - Local 使用拒绝信号来根据每个即时的家族定义二进制标签. 我们通过人工检查每个模型的随机样本来验证这些标签的质量。

blocks.en: For the source prompt and harmful variants, the desired post-patch behaviour is refusal. A response receives label 1 if it is classified as a refusal, and 0 otherwise. Averaging these labels over the source prompt and the 19 harmful variants yields the Harmful Neighbour Correction Score (HNCS) , reported on a 0–100% scale.
blocks.zh: 对于源的即时而有害的变体,所期望的后相行为是拒绝. 如果答复被归类为拒绝,则收到标签1,否则收到0。 在源头上刻出这些标签,19个有害的变体产生有害的邻居校正分数,比例为0-100%。

blocks.en: For benign structural and harmful-word neighbours, the desired behaviour is non-refusal. A response receives label 1 if it is not classified as a refusal, and 0 otherwise. Averaging these labels over the 10 benign neighbours yields the Benign Neighbour Preservation Score (BNPS) , also reported on a 0–100% scale.
blocks.zh: 对于良性的结构性和有害的字眼相邻者,所期望的行为是非反驳的. 如果答复没有被归类为拒绝,则收到标签1,否则收到标签0。 在10个良性邻居身上取出这些标签,

blocks.en: HNCS and BNPS capture complementary failure modes: a low HNCS means the patch fails to induce refusals on the targeted prompt or nearby harmful variants, while a low BNPS means it suppresses too broadly and refuses nearby benign prompts. Reporting both scores separately makes the local repair trade-off explicit.
blocks.zh: HNCS和BNPS捕捉到互补的故障模式:低HNCS表示补丁未能诱发被瞄准的即时或相邻的有害变体上的拒绝,而低BNPS则表示其压制范围过广并拒绝相邻的良性快取. 将两者的分数分别报告,使当地的修理权衡变得明确.

blocks.en: 5 Experimental Protocol and Results
blocks.zh: 5 实验协议和结果

blocks.en: We evaluate four activation patching methods: AlphaSteer, AdaSteer, AST, and CAST, on four models selected from the eight PatchBench model-specific subsets, one per provider: Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, and gemma-3-4b-it. For each model, we use its 50 PatchBench source failures. These failures are model-specific: prompts evaluated for one model are not necessarily the same as those for another, since PatchBench is built from failures actually produced by each model. Additionally, to verify that our observations hold at a larger scale, we evaluated all four methods on a larger Mixture-of-Experts architecture: Llama-4-Scout. These supplementary scaling results are detailed in Appendix D .
blocks.zh: 我们评价四种激活补丁方法:AlphaSteer、AdaSteer、AST和CAST,从8个Patch Bench模型特定子集中选取了4个模型,每个提供者1个:Qun2.5-3B-Instruct、Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3、Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct和Gemma-3-4b-it。 对于每个模型,我们使用它的50 Patch Bench源故障。 这些失败是模式特有的:对一个模型的评价的提示不一定与对另一个模型的评价相同,因为Patch Bench是由每个模型实际产生的失败所建立. 此外,为了核实我们的观察在更大范围内存在,我们评价了更大的专家混合结构的所有四种方法: 拉玛 -4 -斯考特 附录D详述了这些补充按比例调整结果。

blocks.en: All methods are evaluated on the same source failures, generated local neighbourhoods, WildGuard-based scorer, and MMLU 5-shot setup. Hyperparameters are tuned on a held-out validation set and fixed for final evaluation. Implementation details are provided in Appendix F .
blocks.zh: 所有方法都在同一源故障上进行评估,生成了本地街区,基于WildGuard的计分器,以及MMLU 5发的设定. 超参数调整在被搁置的验证装置上,并固定用于最后评价。 执行情况详见附录F。

blocks.en: 5.1 Patching creates a local correction–preservation trade-off
blocks.zh: 5.1 联合国 补丁创建本地更正- 保护权衡

blocks.en: PatchBench-Local evaluates patching where intervention is necessary: the source prompt is a confirmed harmful failure, and the patch is applied to suppress it. The central question is whether this repair remains local: does it induce refusal on the source prompt and nearby harmful variants without over-refusing benign prompts in the same neighbourhood?
blocks.zh: Patch Bench-local评价需要干预的补丁:源出即是确认的有害故障,并应用补丁来压制. 中心问题是这种修复是否仍然是局部的:它是否诱使源头拒绝迅速和相邻的有害变体,而没有在同一街区过度反射出良性诱因?

blocks.en: Figure 5 shows how each method moves a model in the HNCS–BNPS plane relative to its unsteered behaviour. A selective repair should move upward, improving harmful-neighbour correction, while remaining far to the right, preserving benign-neighbour behaviour. In practice, many methods move upward and leftward: they improve correction, but introduce local benign regressions. A complementary aggregate view is provided in Appendix E .
blocks.zh: 图5显示HNCS-BNPS平面中每种方法相对于其未被警告的行为如何移动一个模型. 选择性修复应当向上推进,改善有害邻居矫正,同时保持向右走得更远,保持良性邻居行为. 在实际操作中,许多方法向上走并向后走:它们改善了校正,但引入了局部良性回归. 附录E提供了补充综合视图。

blocks.en: The main pattern is that strong harmful-neighbour correction often comes with substantial benign-neighbour degradation. AST is the clearest example: it frequently obtains the highest HNCS, but its gain over selective methods is modest compared with its BNPS loss. On Qwen 3B, AST improves HNCS over AlphaSteer by only 3.1 points while losing 27.4 BNPS points. On Llama 8B, it nearly matches AdaSteer in HNCS but loses 17.5 BNPS points. On Gemma 4B, it is below AdaSteer in HNCS and 58.3 points lower in BNPS.
blocks.zh: 主要的规律是,强烈的有害-邻居矫正往往伴随着良性的-邻居退化. AST是最明显的例子:它经常获得最高的HNCS,但相对于其BNPS损失,它对选择性方法的得益不大. 在Qwen 3B上,AST比AlphaSteer改进了HNCS,只有3.1分,同时损失了27.4 BNPS分. 在Llama 8B上,它几乎与HNCS的AdaSteer相匹配,但损失了17.5 BNPS分. 在Gemma 4B上,它位于HNCS的AdaSteer以下,而BNPS的分数更低58.3分.

blocks.en: AlphaSteer and AdaSteer provide more favourable correction–preservation profiles on most models. AlphaSteer is particularly strong on Qwen 3B, where it reaches high harmful correction while preserving most benign neighbours. On Gemma 4B, AdaSteer appears more balanced than AST. CAST is generally more conservative, with weaker harmful correction but smaller benign losses than AST on Mistral 7B and Gemma 4B. The highlighted CAST cases in Table 1 will be used in Section 5.2 to compare local benign regressions with global MMLU degradation.
blocks.zh: AlphaSteer 和 AdaSteer 为大多数模型提供了更有利的校正保护配置 。 阿尔法 在Quen 3B上,指导力特别强,它达到高度有害的校正,同时保护了大多数良性邻居. 在Gemma 4B上,AdaSteer显得比AST更平衡. 与米斯特拉尔7B和Gemma4B上的AST相比,CAST一般较为保守,有害的校正较弱但良性损失较小. 表1中突出的CAST案例将在第5.2节中用于比较局部良性回归与全球MMLU降解.

blocks.en: Table 1 : PatchBench-Local results. HNCS measures harmful-neighbour correction and BNPS measures benign-neighbour preservation. Scores are reported on a 0–100 scale (higher is better). Highlighted cells mark the CAST cases discussed in Section 5.2.
blocks.zh: 表1:补丁-当地结果。 HNCS测量有害邻接的校正,BNPS测量无害邻接的保存. 得分按0-100的比例报告(较高者更好)。 第5.2节所讨论CAST案例的突出显示的单元格。

blocks.en: Table 1 confirms that harmful correction and benign preservation must be measured separately. Several methods substantially improve HNCS, but the corresponding BNPS varies widely, showing that successful suppression of harmful variants does not imply a selective repair.
blocks.zh: 表1确认,必须分别衡量有害纠正和无害保全。 几种方法大大地改进了HNCS,但相应的BNPS差别很大,表明成功抑制有害变体并不意味着有选择性地进行修复.

blocks.en: 5.2 Global capability can miss local regressions
blocks.zh: 5.2 全球能力可能错失局部回归

blocks.en: We complement PatchBench-Local with 5-shot MMLU to compare local side effects with global capability preservation. This allows us to test whether benign-neighbour regressions are visible in a standard global capability benchmark.
blocks.zh: 我们用5发MMLU来补充Patch Bench-local,以比较局部副作用和全球能力保护. 这使得我们可以测试在标准的全球能力基准中是否可以看到良邻回归。

blocks.en: Table 2 : MMLU 5-shot accuracy after patching. Values are accuracies in percent; parentheses report percentage-point changes relative to the unsteered model. Highlighted cells mark the CAST cases discussed in Section 5.2.
blocks.zh: 表2:补丁后MMLU5射入精度. 数值以百分比表示;括号中报告的百分比点与未定型模型相比有所变化。 第5.2节所讨论CAST案例的突出显示的单元格。

blocks.en: Key observation. Tables 1 and 2 show that global capability preservation and local benign preservation are not equivalent. The highlighted CAST cases are the clearest example: on Llama 8B and Gemma 4B, MMLU drops by only 0.07 and 0.52 points, while BNPS drops by 26.3 and 22.0 points. The pattern is not specific to CAST: AlphaSteer on Llama 8B and AdaSteer on Qwen 3B also show modest MMLU drops but clear BNPS losses. Conversely, AST illustrates the more obvious case where broad local suppression often coincides with large global capability drops. PatchBench-Local is therefore complementary to MMLU: it diagnoses collateral damage around the repaired failure, even when global capability appears preserved.
blocks.zh: 关键观察. 表1和表2显示,全球能力保护和地方良性保护并不相等。 突出的CAST案例是最明显的例子:在Llama 8B和Gemma 4B上,MMLU只下降了0.07分和0.52分,而BNPS则下降了26.3分和22.0分. 该模式并非CAST所特有:Llama 8B上的AlphaSteer和Quen 3B上的AdaSteer也显示有适度的MMLU下降,但清除了BNPS的损失. 反之,AST说明了一个更明显的例子,即广泛的局部压制往往与全球能力的大幅下降同时发生。 因此,Patch Bench-Local是MMLU的补充:它诊断了修复后故障前后的附带损害,即使全球能力似乎保存了下来.

blocks.en: 5.3 Benign regressions can be lexical, structural, or both
blocks.zh: 5.3 Benign回归可以是词法的,结构的,或者两者兼有.

blocks.en: PatchBench-Local decomposes benign-neighbour losses into two failure modes. Lexical overblocking occurs when a patch refuses benign prompts because they reuse harmful terms. Structural overblocking occurs when it refuses benign prompts because they preserve the scaffold of the harmful request after the harmful intent has been removed.
blocks.zh: Patch Bench - Local 将良-邻损失分解为两种故障模式. 当一补丁因重复使用有害术语而拒绝良性提示时,就会发生表征性过度阻塞. 结构性的过度阻塞在拒绝良性提示时发生,因为它们在有害意图被移除后保留了有害请求的脚手架.

blocks.en: Figure 6 shows that benign regressions differ not only in magnitude, but also in kind. AlphaSteer on Llama 8B has low lexical loss but high structural loss, suggesting over-generalisation from the form of the request rather than from harmful words. AdaSteer shows a more mixed profile, with substantial lexical loss on Llama 8B but milder losses on Mistral 7B and Gemma 4B. CAST also varies by model, with low benign loss on Mistral 7B, larger structural loss on Llama 8B, and larger lexical loss on Gemma 4B.
blocks.zh: 图6显示,良性回归不仅在规模上不同,在实物上也不同. 阿尔法 指挥Llama 8B有低字法损失而高结构损失,表明从请求的形式而不是从有害的词来过度概括. AdaSteer显示的情况比较好坏参半,在Llama 8B上出现了大量的词汇损失,但在Mistral 7B和Gemma 4B上则出现了更轻微的损失. CAST也因型号而异,米斯特拉尔7B的良性损失较低,拉玛8B的结构性损失较大,而Gemma4B的辞典损失较大.

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en: We introduced PatchBench, a curated benchmark of model-specific jailbreak failures, and PatchBench-Local, a local evaluation protocol for activation patching. Together, they turn jailbreak repair into a concrete local question: does a patch suppress the targeted failure and its nearby harmful variants while preserving lexically and structurally related benign prompts?
blocks.zh: 我们引入了Patch Bench, 一个特定模式的越狱失败的解析基准, 以及Patch Bench-Local, 一个激活补丁的本地评价协议。 他们共同将越狱修复变成一个具体的局部问题:一个补丁是否抑制了有针对性的失败及其附近的有害变体,同时保留了与逻辑和结构相关的良性诱因?

blocks.en: Our experiments show that this distinction matters. Activation patching can substantially improve harmful-neighbour correction, but the same interventions may also induce strong benign-neighbour regressions, including when global capability metrics such as MMLU remain nearly unchanged. Methods that appear effective under harmful correction alone can therefore behave as broad local suppressors rather than selective repairs.
blocks.zh: 我们的实验表明,这种区别很重要。 激活补丁可大大地改进有害-邻接的校正,但同样的干预措施也可能诱发强烈的良性-邻接回归,包括当MMLU等全球能力指标几乎保持不变时。 因此,仅仅在有害的矫正下看来有效的方法就能够作为广泛的局部抑制器而不是选择性的修复。

blocks.en: PatchBench provides an initial testbed for measuring this correction–preservation trade-off. The central lesson is that an activation patch should not merely suppress unsafe behaviour; it should repair it locally.
blocks.zh: Patch Bench 提供了用于测量这种校正-保护取舍的初始测试床。 中心教训是,激活补丁不应仅仅压制不安全的行为;它应在当地修复。

blocks.en: 7 Broader impacts and limitations
blocks.zh: 第7条 更广泛的影响和限制

blocks.en: PatchBench contains harmful prompts and actionable model completions, creating dual-use risks. We release them because concrete failures are necessary to evaluate activation patching and expose safety weaknesses reproducibly. To reduce misuse, the release includes documentation, safety warnings, a non-commercial license, and an intended-use statement focused on defensive research, benchmarking, and red-teaming evaluation.
blocks.zh: Patch Bench载有有害的提示和可操作的模型完成,造成了双重用途的风险。 我们释放它们是因为需要具体的失败来评估激活补丁并重复暴露安全弱点。 为了减少误用,发布内容包括文件、安全警告、非商业许可证以及侧重于防御研究、基准和红色团队评价的用途说明。

blocks.en:
PatchBench trades breadth for precision. It is not intended to cover all jailbreak strategies, harmful domains, or model behaviours, nor to certify broad robustness. Likewise, MMLU provides only a coarse global capability check and does not replace task-specific utility evaluation. Current activation patching methods also remain sensitive to hyperparameter choices, which can affect both harmful-neighbour correction and benign-neighbour preservation. We therefore tune all methods under a shared validation protocol and release our implementations to support reproducibility and fair comparison.
Finally, extending the benchmark to new models requires manual, model-specific generation. We see this one-time cost as a necessary trade-off to expose architecture-specific side effects, which is fully amortised when testing multiple repair methods.
blocks.zh:
帕奇·本奇用宽度交换精度 它的目的不是要涵盖所有越狱战略、有害领域或示范行为,也不是要证明广泛的稳健性。 同样,MMLU只提供粗糙的全球能力检查,并不取代特定任务的效用评价. 目前的激活补丁方法对超参数选择也依然敏感,这既会影响有害-邻居的矫正,也会影响良性-邻居的保存. 因此,我们根据共同的验证协议调整所有方法,并公布我们的执行情况,以支持可复制性和公平比较性。
最后,将基准扩大到新的模型需要人工的,针对模型的生成. 我们认为,这种一次性成本是暴露建筑特有副作用的一种必要的取舍,在测试多种维修方法时,这种副作用是完全摊还的.

blocks.en: A central direction for future work is to study how local repair metrics should scale beyond isolated neighbourhoods. When many failures are considered simultaneously, the challenge is not only to improve average correction, but also to detect interference between local regions and accumulated benign regressions across them. Designing metrics that preserve this locality while summarising many repair neighbourhoods is essential for evaluating activation patching as a reliable safety intervention.
blocks.zh: 未来工作的一个中心方向是研究当地修理指标应如何超越孤立的街区。 当同时考虑许多失败时,挑战不仅在于改进平均更正,而且在于发现局部区域之间的干扰和相互间累积的良性回归。 设计保护该地段的衡量标准,同时总结许多维修区,对于将激活补丁作为一种可靠的安全干预措施进行评估至关重要。

blocks.en: C.1 Generation Prompt

blocks.en: PatchBench-Local generates local neighbourhoods using Mistral Large with a fixed prompt template. Given a PatchBench source prompt, the generator returns a strict JSON object with three groups: harmful variants, benign structural neighbours, and benign harmful-word neighbours. We use the following template for all source prompts.

conducted a supplementary study: we regenerated the local neighbourhoods using GPT-4o and re-ran the evaluation on the resulting dataset. Table 5 and Table 6 compare the HNCS and BNPS metrics obtained using our default Mistral Large generator against those from GPT-4o. The results are consistent across both generators. As shown in Table 5 , this variance causes some minor ranking inversions between methods with closely tied scores. Appendix F Patching Methods Implementation Details We describe the practical implementation of the four patching methods evaluated. All methods are integrated into the same training, validation, inference, and WildGuard-based labelling pipeline. Method-specific artefacts, such as refusal vectors, condition vectors, or projection matrices, are trained on the training split. Steering hyperparameters are then selected on a held-out validation split, which is disjoint from both the training data and the final test prompts. The validation and test splits contain prompts from four distinct categories: original harmful prompts identified as causing response failures for the evaluated model and the three local prompt families introduced in Section 4, namely close harmful variants, benign prompts containing close harmful words and benign prompts with the same structure as the original harmful prompts. For each category, we compute a success score: the refusal rate for harmful prompts and the acceptance rate for benign prompts. We then average these metrics to obtain a single discriminative score used to select the best hyperparameter configuration. F.1 AST Activation Steering (AST) [ 12 ] is implemented as an unconditional refusal steering method. It learns a single refusal vector intended to increase the model’s propensity to refuse. We use AST as a control method to illustrate that unconditional steering can achieve high refusal rates on harmful prompts but also noticeably degrades performance on benign prompts. The refusal vector is trained from benign prompts paired with refusal and compliance suffixes. Given a prompt x x , it constructs two contrastive inputs: ( x + s refusal , x + s compliant ) (x+s_{\mathrm{refusal}},\;x+s_{\mathrm{compliant}}) where s refusal s_{\mathrm{refusal}} is a suffix inducing refusal behaviour and s compliant s_{\mathrm{compliant}} is the corresponding compliant suffix. Since the user prompt is identical across both inputs, the extracted direction primarily captures the difference between refusal and compliance behaviour. We reproduce the implementation of [ 12 ] to share the same structure with CAST: we use the same benign Alpaca prompts and suffixes to construct the contrastive pairs. For each transformer layer, hidden states are extracted from the suffix tokens and centred pairwise. A one-dimensional PCA is then fitted to these centred activations to capture a layer-wise refusal direction. During inference, the refusal vector is added to the activations at the selected layers and scaled by a steering strength chosen on the validation set. h ′ ( l ) ← h ( l ) + α ​ r ( l ) h^{\prime(l)}\leftarrow h^{(l)}+\alpha\,r^{(l)} where r ( l ) r^{(l)} denotes the fitted refusal direction for layer l l . Refusal steering is applied to the middle half of the transformer layers, excluding the first and last quarters. We found this to be a strong heuristic for refusal performance, while substantially reducing the size of the validation grid search. Table 9 reports the refusal steering strength selected for each evaluated model. The steering strength is chosen on the validation set to maximise refusal on harmful prompts while limiting degradation in response quality. F.2 CAST Conditional Activation Steering (CAST) [ 12 ] extends AST by making refusal steering conditional. It uses the same refusal vector as AST, along with the refusal activation strength scalar selected on the AST validation set. This gives CAST the same refusal steering direction as AST, when the condition gating is activated. CAST learns a condition vector from contrastive safe/unsafe prompt pairs. Unsafe prompts are collected separately for each model from PatchBench. We first select harmful prompts that the model fails to refuse, since these correspond to the behaviour we aim to patch. For some models, this provides only a few hundred prompts. To standardise the dataset size across models, we augment it with additional harmful prompts sampled from PatchBench, resulting in 1500 1500 contrastive pairs per model. For the safe prompts, we reuse the Alpaca prompts from the original CAST method. After computing the condition vector c c , CAST compares the hidden state h h at the selected condition layer with its projection onto c c , producing a score that measures how strongly the prompt matches the learned unsafe condition. A validation-selected gate, specified by a layer, threshold θ \theta and comparison direction, determines whether the condition is active. If the gate is satisfied, CAST applies the refusal vector r r at the selected behaviour layers following the condition layer, using the same intervention as AST. Otherwise, generation proceeds without refusal steering. h ′ ( l ) ← h ( l ) + α 𝟏 [ sim ( h ( l ) , proj c h ( l ) ) > θ ] r ( l ) h^{\prime(l)}\leftarrow h^{(l)}+\alpha\mathbf{1}\left[\,\text{sim}(h^{(l)},\text{proj}_{c}h^{(l)})>\theta\,\right]r^{(l)} As in the original CAST method, we perform a grid-search on our validation set over the condition gating hyperparameters: the condition layer, threshold θ \theta and the inequality direction. We select the conditional configuration that maximises the F 1 F_{1} score for distinguishing harmful from benign validation prompts. We then use this fixed gate during the standard validation procedure for the remaining hyperparameters.

Claims Question: Do the main claims made in the abstract and introduction accurately reflect the paper’s contributions and scope? Answer: [Yes] . Justification: The abstract and introduction state the two main contributions, PatchBench and PatchBench-Local, and the experimental claim that harmful-neighbour correction can coincide with benign-neighbour regressions. These claims are supported by Sections 3–5 and by the limitations discussed in Section 7. 2. Limitations Question: Does the paper discuss the limitations of the work performed by the authors? Answer: [Yes] . Justification: Section 7 discusses the scope of PatchBench, the fact that it trades breadth for precision, and the interpretation of PatchBench-Local as a local diagnostic rather than a broad robustness certificate. It also discusses future work on scaling local repair metrics beyond isolated neighbourhoods. 3. Theory assumptions and proofs Question: For each theoretical result, does the paper provide the full set of assumptions and a complete (and correct) proof? Answer: [N/A] . Justification: The paper does not introduce theoretical results, theorems, or formal proofs. Its contributions are a benchmark, a local evaluation protocol, and empirical evaluations of activation patching methods. 4. Experimental result reproducibility Question: Does the paper fully disclose all the information needed to reproduce the main experimental results of the paper to the extent that it affects the main claims and/or conclusions of the paper (regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not)? Answer: [Yes] . Justification: Sections 3–5 describe the benchmark construction, local neighbourhood generation, scoring protocol, evaluated models, patching methods, and metrics. Appendix A provides data and code availability, Section C.1 gives the local generation prompt, and Appendix F describes the patching method implementations. 5. Open access to data and code Question: Does the paper provide open access to the data and code, with sufficient instructions to faithfully reproduce the main experimental results, as described in supplemental material? Answer: [Yes] . Justification: Appendix A states that the PatchBench data and accompanying code are publicly available, and that the full data-processing and benchmark pipeline can be reproduced end to end using the repository instructions. 6. Experimental setting/details Question: Does the paper specify all the training and test details (e.g., data splits, hyperparameters, how they were chosen, type of optimizer) necessary to understand the results? Answer: [Yes] . Justification: Section 5 describes the evaluated models, source failures, local neighbourhoods, WildGuard scorer, MMLU setup, and held-out hyperparameter tuning. Appendix F gives implementation details for the patching methods, including validation-based hyperparameter selection and method-specific artefacts. 7. Experiment statistical significance Question: Does the paper report error bars suitably and correctly defined or other appropriate information about the statistical significance of the experiments? Answer: [No] . Justification: We do not report error bars because the main results are deterministic benchmark measurements rather than averages over stochastic training runs. For each model and method, PatchBench-Local is evaluated on a fixed set of 50 source failures, fixed generated neighbourhoods, deterministic decoding, and a shared WildGuard-based scorer. The reported HNCS and BNPS values are therefore exact scores on this evaluation set, analogous to reporting accuracy on a fixed benchmark split. The main source of variation relevant to our claims is not random seed variability, but heterogeneity across models, patching methods, and benign-neighbour families; we expose this variation explicitly in Table 1 and Figures 5 – 6 . 8. Answer: [Yes] . Justification: Appendix A reports the main compute resources used for benchmark construction and evaluation, including the 4 NVIDIA A100 GPUs used for large-scale inference and Elo ranking and the 2 NVIDIA H100 GPUs used for Llama-4-Scout inference. 9. Justification: The work is designed to support defensive safety research and reproducible evaluation of LLM repair methods. Justification: Section 7 and Appendix A discuss the positive impact of exposing and repairing safety weaknesses, as well as the dual-use risks associated with releasing harmful prompts and actionable model completions. 11. Answer: [Yes] . Justification: Appendix A describes the intended defensive use of the dataset, the licence, attribution requirements, and the discouragement of using the dataset to train models to comply with harmful requests. Answer: [Yes] . Answer: [Yes] . Justification: LLMs are used as part of the core methodology: Mistral Large generates local neighbourhoods, WildGuard provides refusal and safety labels, and an LLM judge is used for pairwise Elo ranking during benchmark curation. blocks.en: C.2 Comparison of LLM Generators for PatchBench-Local
blocks.zh: C.2 补丁-当地雇员LLM发电机比较

blocks.en: To verify the robustness of our local prompt generation protocol against potential LLM biases, we conducted a supplementary study: we regenerated the local neighbourhoods using GPT-4o and re-ran the evaluation on the resulting dataset. Table 5 and Table 6 compare the HNCS and BNPS metrics obtained using our default Mistral Large generator against those from GPT-4o. The results are consistent across both generators. Although GPT-4o prompts yield slightly lower refusal rates, the differences are marginal. As shown in Table 5 , this variance causes some minor ranking inversions between methods with closely tied scores. However, Table 6 confirms that the overall method rankings remain perfectly stable once aggregated, demonstrating that our evaluation protocol is not overly sensitive to the choice of the generating LLM.

blocks.en: Appendix D Scaling to Larger Models: Evaluation on Llama-4-Scout
blocks.zh: 附录D 放大到更大的模型:对Llama-4-Scout的评价

blocks.en: To verify whether the patterns observed on 3B–14B models scale to larger architectures, we evaluated all four patching methods on Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct, a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model with 109B total parameters. As shown in Table 7 , the same central trade-off remains visible on this substantially larger model: methods that achieve the strongest harmfulness reduction can also incur a considerable loss of benign performance. For example, AlphaSteer achieves the highest HNCS but the lowest BNPS, whereas AST and CAST preserve substantially more benign performance while obtaining smaller HNCS gains. While this additional experiment does not establish a universal scaling law, it provides clear evidence that the fundamental trade-off identified by PatchBench-Local is not restricted to small dense models, but also arises in a substantially larger MoE architecture.
blocks.zh: 为了验证在3B–14B模型上所观测到的图案是否尺度到更大的架构,我们评价了Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct上的所有四种补丁方法,一种具有109B总参数的"专家混合"模型. 如表7所显示的,在这个大得多的模型上仍然可以看到同样的中心取舍:实现最强烈的有害性降低的方法也可能造成相当程度的良性性能损失. 例如,AlphaSteer取得了最高的HNCS但最低的BNPS,而AST和CAST则在取得较小的HNCS增益的同时保持了显著的良性性能. 虽然这个额外的实验没有确立一个通用的缩放法,但它提供了明确的证据,表明帕奇·本克-勒克特(Patch Bench-Local)确定的基本取舍并不限于小密集型号,而且还出现在一个大得多的教育部架构中.

blocks.en: Appendix F Patching Methods Implementation Details
blocks.zh: 附录F 补丁 实施细节

blocks.en: We describe the practical implementation of the four patching methods evaluated. All methods are integrated into the same training, validation, inference, and WildGuard-based labelling pipeline. Method-specific artefacts, such as refusal vectors, condition vectors, or projection matrices, are trained on the training split. Steering hyperparameters are then selected on a held-out validation split, which is disjoint from both the training data and the final test prompts. The validation and test splits contain prompts from four distinct categories: original harmful prompts identified as causing response failures for the evaluated model and the three local prompt families introduced in Section 4, namely close harmful variants, benign prompts containing close harmful words and benign prompts with the same structure as the original harmful prompts. For each category, we compute a success score: the refusal rate for harmful prompts and the acceptance rate for benign prompts. We then average these metrics to obtain a single discriminative score used to select the best hyperparameter configuration.
blocks.zh: 我们描述了所评价的四种补丁方法的实际执行情况。 所有方法都融入同一个培训、验证、推论和基于WildGuard的标签管道。 特定方法的工艺品,如拒绝载体、条件载体或投影矩阵,都经过训练分解。 然后在搁置的验证分解上选择方向超参数,该分解与培训数据和最后测试提示不相干。 鉴定和测试分解包含来自四个不同类别的提示:被评估模型被确认为造成反应失败的原始有害提示和在第4节中引入的三个当地提示家庭,即近有害变体、含有近有害词的良性提示和结构与原始有害提示相同的良性提示。 对于每一个类别,我们计算一个成功的分数:有害分数的拒绝率和良性分数的接受率。 然后,我们平均这些度量衡,以获得一个用于选择最佳超参数配置的单一分数。

blocks.en: Activation Steering (AST) [ 12 ] is implemented as an unconditional refusal steering method. It learns a single refusal vector intended to increase the model’s propensity to refuse. We use AST as a control method to illustrate that unconditional steering can achieve high refusal rates on harmful prompts but also noticeably degrades performance on benign prompts. The refusal vector is trained from benign prompts paired with refusal and compliance suffixes. Given a prompt x x , it constructs two contrastive inputs: ( x + s refusal , x + s compliant ) (x+s_{\mathrm{refusal}},\;x+s_{\mathrm{compliant}}) where s refusal s_{\mathrm{refusal}} is a suffix inducing refusal behaviour and s compliant s_{\mathrm{compliant}} is the corresponding compliant suffix. Since the user prompt is identical across both inputs, the extracted direction primarily captures the difference between refusal and compliance behaviour. We reproduce the implementation of [ 12 ] to share the same structure with CAST: we use the same benign Alpaca prompts and suffixes to construct the contrastive pairs. For each transformer layer, hidden states are extracted from the suffix tokens and centred pairwise. A one-dimensional PCA is then fitted to these centred activations to capture a layer-wise refusal direction. During inference, the refusal vector is added to the activations at the selected layers and scaled by a steering strength chosen on the validation set. h ′ ( l ) ← h ( l ) + α ​ r ( l ) h^{\prime(l)}\leftarrow h^{(l)}+\alpha\,r^{(l)} where r ( l ) r^{(l)} denotes the fitted refusal direction for layer l l . Refusal steering is applied to the middle half of the transformer layers, excluding the first and last quarters. We found this to be a strong heuristic for refusal performance, while substantially reducing the size of the validation grid search. Table 9 reports the refusal steering strength selected for each evaluated model. The steering strength is chosen on the validation set to maximise refusal on harmful prompts while limiting degradation in response quality.

AdaSteer [ 26 ] is an adaptive activation steering method that
extends single-direction refusal steering with a second, harmfulness-related
direction. Rather than applying a fixed steering coefficient to a single refusal

the rejection vector on prompts that the model should comply with. The per-prompt coefficients are produced by two affine calibrations fitted on
held-out prompts. We integrate AdaSteer in our pipeline by re-using the same
training, validation, test inference and WildGuard-based labelling stages
described above, only replacing the artefact trained at the patching stage.

blocks.en: NeurIPS Paper Checklist
blocks.zh: 神经病 纸张核对表

blocks.en: 1. Claims Question: Do the main claims made in the abstract and introduction accurately reflect the paper’s contributions and scope? Answer: [Yes] . Justification: The abstract and introduction state the two main contributions, PatchBench and PatchBench-Local, and the experimental claim that harmful-neighbour correction can coincide with benign-neighbour regressions. These claims are supported by Sections 3–5 and by the limitations discussed in Section 7. 2. Limitations Question: Does the paper discuss the limitations of the work performed by the authors? Answer: [Yes] . Justification: Section 7 discusses the scope of PatchBench, the fact that it trades breadth for precision, and the interpretation of PatchBench-Local as a local diagnostic rather than a broad robustness certificate. It also discusses future work on scaling local repair metrics beyond isolated neighbourhoods. 3. Theory assumptions and proofs Question: For each theoretical result, does the paper provide the full set of assumptions and a complete (and correct) proof? Answer: [N/A] . Justification: The paper does not introduce theoretical results, theorems, or formal proofs. Its contributions are a benchmark, a local evaluation protocol, and empirical evaluations of activation patching methods. 4. Experimental result reproducibility Question: Does the paper fully disclose all the information needed to reproduce the main experimental results of the paper to the extent that it affects the main claims and/or conclusions of the paper (regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not)? Answer: [Yes] . Justification: Sections 3–5 describe the benchmark construction, local neighbourhood generation, scoring protocol, evaluated models, patching methods, and metrics. Appendix A provides data and code availability, Section C.1 gives the local generation prompt, and Appendix F describes the patching method implementations. 5. Open access to data and code Question: Does the paper provide open access to the data and code, with sufficient instructions to faithfully reproduce the main experimental results, as described in supplemental material? Answer: [Yes] . Justification: Appendix A states that the PatchBench data and accompanying code are publicly available, and that the full data-processing and benchmark pipeline can be reproduced end to end using the repository instructions. 6. Experimental setting/details Question: Does the paper specify all the training and test details (e.g., data splits, hyperparameters, how they were chosen, type of optimizer) necessary to understand the results? Answer: [Yes] . Justification: Section 5 describes the evaluated models, source failures, local neighbourhoods, WildGuard scorer, MMLU setup, and held-out hyperparameter tuning. Appendix F gives implementation details for the patching methods, including validation-based hyperparameter selection and method-specific artefacts. 7. Experiment statistical significance Question: Does the paper report error bars suitably and correctly defined or other appropriate information about the statistical significance of the experiments? Answer: [No] . Justification: We do not report error bars because the main results are deterministic benchmark measurements rather than averages over stochastic training runs. For each model and method, PatchBench-Local is evaluated on a fixed set of 50 source failures, fixed generated neighbourhoods, deterministic decoding, and a shared WildGuard-based scorer. The reported HNCS and BNPS values are therefore exact scores on this evaluation set, analogous to reporting accuracy on a fixed benchmark split. The main source of variation relevant to our claims is not random seed variability, but heterogeneity across models, patching methods, and benign-neighbour families; we expose this variation explicitly in Table 1 and Figures 5 – 6 . 8. Experiments compute resources Question: For each experiment, does the paper provide sufficient information on the computer resources (type of compute workers, memory, time of execution) needed to reproduce the experiments? Answer: [Yes] . Justification: Appendix A reports the main compute resources used for benchmark construction and evaluation, including the 4 NVIDIA A100 GPUs used for large-scale inference and Elo ranking and the 2 NVIDIA H100 GPUs used for Llama-4-Scout inference. 9. Code of ethics Question: Does the research conducted in the paper conform, in every respect, with the NeurIPS Code of Ethics https://neurips.cc/public/EthicsGuidelines ? Answer: [Yes] . Justification: The work is designed to support defensive safety research and reproducible evaluation of LLM repair methods. Section 7 and Appendix A discuss dual-use risks, intended use, data release, ethics, and safeguards against misuse. 10. Broader impacts Question: Does the paper discuss both potential positive societal impacts and negative societal impacts of the work performed? Answer: [Yes] . Justification: Section 7 and Appendix A discuss the positive impact of exposing and repairing safety weaknesses, as well as the dual-use risks associated with releasing harmful prompts and actionable model completions. 11. Safeguards Question: Does the paper describe safeguards that have been put in place for responsible release of data or models that have a high risk for misuse (e.g., pre-trained language models, image generators, or scraped datasets)? Answer: [Yes] . Justification: Appendix A describes the intended defensive use of the dataset, the licence, attribution requirements, and the discouragement of using the dataset to train models to comply with harmful requests. The paper also explicitly discusses dual-use risks in Section 7. 12. Licenses for existing assets Question: Are the creators or original owners of assets (e.g., code, data, models), used in the paper, properly credited and are the license and terms of use explicitly mentioned and properly respected? Answer: [Yes] . Justification: Appendix A.2 describes the licences of the source data used to construct PatchBench, including RED-Bench and Stanford Alpaca-derived data, and states the licence chosen for the released PatchBench dataset and accompanying source code. 13. New assets Question: Are new assets introduced in the paper well documented and is the documentation provided alongside the assets? Answer: [Yes] . Justification: The paper introduces PatchBench and PatchBench-Local as new benchmark assets. Sections 3–4 document their construction and evaluation protocol, while Appendix A provides release information and Section C.1 provides the local neighbourhood generation prompt. 14. Crowdsourcing and research with human subjects Question: For crowdsourcing experiments and research with human subjects, does the paper include the full text of instructions given to participants and screenshots, if applicable, as well as details about compensation (if any)? Answer: [N/A] . Justification: The paper does not involve crowdsourcing experiments or research with human subjects. Manual review is performed by the authors as part of benchmark curation. 15. Institutional review board (IRB) approvals or equivalent for research with human subjects Question: Does the paper describe potential risks incurred by study participants, whether such risks were disclosed to the subjects, and whether Institutional Review Board (IRB) approvals (or an equivalent approval/review based on the requirements of your country or institution) were obtained? Answer: [N/A] . Justification: The paper does not involve human subjects research, personal records, or participant data. Therefore, IRB approval or equivalent review for human subjects research is not applicable. 16. Declaration of LLM usage Question: Does the paper describe the usage of LLMs if it is an important, original, or non-standard component of the core methods in this research? Note that if the LLM is used only for writing, editing, or formatting purposes and does not impact the core methodology, scientific rigor, or originality of the research, declaration is not required. Answer: [Yes] . Justification: LLMs are used as part of the core methodology: Mistral Large generates local neighbourhoods, WildGuard provides refusal and safety labels, and an LLM judge is used for pairwise Elo ranking during benchmark curation. These uses are described in Sections 3–5 and Section C.1 .
